neighbours.label: a word naming an economic sector just before 'industry', 'sector' or 'business' (the travel industry, the hotel business), as opposed to the same noun as an ordinary object or place
fire: My uncle has spent thirty years in the insurance industry.
Workers in the tourism sector lost their jobs during the storm.
Her book describes how the music business changed after the internet.
New rules will affect the shipping industry from next spring.
He made his fortune in the textile business before the war.
The minister met leaders of the mining sector on Friday.
Women are still rare at the top of the steel industry.
Critics say the tobacco industry has hidden the data for years.
quiet: My uncle has kept thirty letters from the insurance clerk.
Children on the tourism bus lost their hats during the storm.
Her book describes how the music teacher changed after the wedding.
New curtains will brighten the shipping office from next spring.
He tore his coat on the textile loom before the race.
The minister wore a helmet from the mining museum on Friday.
Cats are still rare at the top of the steel tower.
Critics say the tobacco leaf has dried in the barn for years.

short: word naming a business sector (the travel industry)
notes: Output: promotes industry, sector, hospitality on this pole. Card: ' the' x16 before such words, ' food', ' seafood'. Probes: travel 1.03, oil and gas sector 0.88, food 0.64, fashion 0.56, auto 0.49, hotel business 0.39, banking 0.34, sugar 0.29; hotel downtown 0.01, sugar farmer 0.08. The ' the' itself fires in any business-like frame ('experience in the small town' 0.66, 'Jobs in the northern town' 0.50, 'been in the old building' 0.54), so my near misses leave those frames, and this test cannot speak to that part of the pole.
